source.title: When Personalization Legitimizes Risks: Uncovering Safety Vulnerabilities in Personalized Dialogue Agents
source.authors: Jiahe Guo; Xiangran Guo; Yu-Lin Hu; Zi-Mo Long; Xing-Yu Sui; X. Zhi; Yong-Bo Huang; Hao He; Weixiang Zhao; Yan-Yan Zhao; Bing Qin

page_placements.theme: Demonstrations, conversation history and memory alter safety

record.file_problem: Some table and figure content is flattened or garbled in the extracted text; the paper text is otherwise present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether benign personalized context increases harmful-response rates, using retrieved memories rather than fine-tuning. This is a different method aimed at a closely related safety-erosion question.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates benign memory retrieval and personalization, not fine-tuning on benign or harmful examples. It reports ASR results for stateless and personalized agents, memory-volume and PII variations, thematic context, and an inference-time mitigation. It does not measure KL by response position, compliant-prefix attacks, suffixes, decoding changes, parameter localization, or training-objective explanations.
record.test_reason: This study measures how benign personal memories retrieved into the prompt at inference raise harmful compliance in memory-augmented agents. No model is fine-tuned, on harmful or benign data. There is no per-token KL, no prefill, suffix or decoding attack, no parameter localization, no account of shallowness from data or objective, and no deepening training. V2 names benign fine-tuning, and in-context benign context is a different operation, so no row bears on any version. The finding is recorded under fits_no_version. Qi et al. 2406.05946 is cited only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors claim mechanistic evidence: Qwen3-8B representations of harmful queries shift toward benign anchors under memory. Add that the intervention cuts ASR by about 27% on average with framework-dependent utility cost; Amem LoCoMo F1 drops 18.6%.
record.recipe_differences: This study tests adding or retrieving benign personal memories at inference, not the original studies' fine-tuning or token-position interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies with memory framework and representation, memory volume, semantic alignment between memory themes and harmful queries, persona/query composition, and explicit PII availability.

fits_no_version.finding: Retrieving benign, non-poisoned user memories into the prompt raises harmful-query ASR above a stateless baseline for all 5 models and 5 memory frameworks (+15.8% to +243.7% relative). The rise grows with retrieved-memory count, concentrates where memory theme aligns with query category, and is amplified by explicit persona fields. A PCA of Qwen3-8B representations shows harmful queries shifting toward the benign side.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign in-context personal context (not fine-tuning) erodes refusal in safety-aligned models (in-context analogue of V2).

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper notes that some dialogue histories and persona-grounded queries are synthesized, that it does not cover the full range of memory designs, and that evaluation is text-based and single-turn. The human agreement check covers 160 responses; the main ASR tables do not report uncertainty estimates. Some detailed figure values are not reliably recoverable from the extracted text.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted category-by-category Table 1 results, individual persona results in Tables 5–6, and most Table 4 thematic-augmentation cells to keep the record focused on aggregate safety outcomes and within the row limit. Table 4 and Figures 3, 12–14 contain thematic/category-specific results; Tables 5–6 contain persona-specific PS-Bench-Hard results.

untested.parts: All: no benign fine-tuning; only in-context benign memories.
All: no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
All: the mitigation is an inference-time prompt reminder, not deepening training.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 link conflates in-context benign memory with benign fine-tuning. The PII rows' baselines were misaligned by one column in the flattened Table 9 and need correction; with correct values, Qwen3-235B LDAgent decreases (25.8 to 23.8). The study is a T6 for this phenomenon but a candidate source for a separate in-context or personalization safety-erosion claim.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and refusal loss after fine-tuning.
The study tests benign personal memories retrieved at inference, not ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction fine-tuning.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes.
Whether safety behaviour is localized in a small set of parameters or ranks.
Whether training data or objectives produce shallow safety behaviour.
Training to deepen safety across response tokens and whether that improvement persists.

relation.reason: Section 5 cites Qi et al. (2024) as background on post-training safety alignment; the experiments neither test nor use its shallow-alignment finding.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure inference-time conditioning on benign personal memories, which tests none of V1–V7. The representation analysis and inference-time mitigation also do not test these versions.

source_check.notes: All five numerical comparisons match Table 1. The statement's 15.8% lower endpoint comes from GPT-4o-mini with Mem0, outside the five cited LDAgent rows; the full table supports the stated range.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Average ASR in the PS-Bench base setting across the five tested model backbones and personalized-agent frameworks
reader_labels.reason: All reported personalized-agent averages in Table 1 exceed their model's stateless baseline; rows T1-G4o-LDA through T1-DS-MemU report those comparisons.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Privacy-leakage queries and varying retrieved-memory volume
reader_labels.reason: The paper says privacy degradation depends on PII being present; adding PII increases ASR, but the increase is small for GPT-4o-mini with LDAgent. Memory-volume results also show lower ASR at k=1 than at larger k, with that condition only partially above stateless.
